The 2026 United States House of Representatives elections in Arizona will be held on November 3, 2026, to elect nine U.S. representatives from the state of Arizona, one from each of the state's congressional districts. The elections will coincide with other elections to the House of Representatives, elections to the United States Senate, and various state and local elections. The primary elections took place on July 21, 2026.[1]

The 1st district is based in the northeastern Phoenix suburbs, including Scottsdale. The incumbent is Republican David Schweikert, who was reelected with 51.9% of the vote in 2024.[2] Schweikert initially ran for reelection, but withdrew from the race in September 2025 to run for governor.[3]
